title: TOPIC-PARTITION-20NG: on a corpus with ground-truth topic labels the construction has never seen (20 Newsgroups, 20 labels under 7 groups), does the anchor-free recipe of record build and certify, partition the embedding space better than k-means / Ward / HDBSCAN at the same number of parts, and identify topics at its certified sites? (zero judge calls; 1 ingest + 1 smoke build + 2 constructions + 2 site nulls [+ 1 contingency pair]; embeddings local; plan Amendment 8)
question: Q1 (partition): at the same number of parts, does the certified taxonomy partition the embedding space better than k-means (held-out NMI at 20 labels, paired against k-means seed 0 at k = the tree's leaf count)? Q2 (topics): does certification select the topic-aligned sites once depth is held fixed (depth-stratified certified - uncertified NMI_20 gap, permutation p within depth strata), and is the depth-1 split a coarse-group split? Q3 (transfer): does the recipe of record (R1 af_clean_s42: bar 0.025 at the 256-dim slice) build on 20NG with > 20 leaves and certify the root and at least one depth-1 site, and does the FRAMEWORK per-corpus pair (512 / 0.0145) build as well?

plain_description.what: The tree-building recipe was run on 20 Newsgroups, a text corpus with 20 known topic labels the method never saw. The test checked whether the recipe builds and certifies a tree, whether it splits the space better than k-means, Ward or HDBSCAN with the same number of parts, and whether its certified splits line up with the true topics.
plain_description.why: It tests on ground truth whether the discovered tree reflects real structure and is better than plain clustering.
plain_description.information: Beating k-means would show the tree finds better structure. Certified splits lining up with the topics would support trusting the certificate. Result: done. The recipe builds and certifies on this corpus. It splits the space no better than k-means with the same number of parts. Certified splits are somewhat more topic-aligned (p about 0.05), but this rests on few effective sites and does not survive a control for cluster size. One embedder, one seed, one split.
